cards.text: Proverbs starts a new section here, and the teacher talks right to the listener: "Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise." Apply your mind, the teacher says, to my knowledge. Friend, that is the oldest way on record of saying PUT THE PHONE DOWN.

cards.question: The teacher says it's pleasing to keep these words within you and also on your lips.

cards.text: Then the teacher gets personal: "I instruct you today—yes, you." YES, YOU, friend, not the guy in the back row pretending to take notes.

cards.question: The teacher says all this instruction has a goal. What is it?

answers.text: So your trust may be in the LORD
So your name will be remembered
So your barns will be full

cards.text: The teacher has written thirty sayings about counsel and knowledge, to show true and reliable words. THIRTY, friend, and the expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with had exactly one saying, and it expired before I got there.

cards.question: These true and reliable words will also help the listener soundly answer whom?

cards.text: Now the sayings begin. Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate.

cards.question: Don't rob the poor or crush the afflicted at the gate, because the ___ will take up their case.

cards.text: And the LORD will plunder those who rob them. Next saying: do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man.

cards.question: Why steer clear of the hot-tempered man, the guy who honks for three straight miles when somebody cuts him off?

answers.text: You may learn his ways and get caught in a snare
He will spread your secrets and ruin your good name
He will borrow your money and never pay it back

cards.text: Next: do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts. Friend, that's co-signing, putting your name on somebody else's loan.

cards.question: If you put up security for a debt and have nothing to pay with, what does the teacher say could be taken?

answers.text: Your own bed from under you
Your seat at the city gate

cards.text: Next, the teacher turns to land, and the ancient boundary stone your fathers placed.

cards.question: The teacher says moving that ancient boundary stone is fine if you need more room.

cards.text: Then the teacher asks, "Do you see a man skilled in his work?" Not the one who says "let's circle back" in every meeting, friend, the one who actually gets it DONE.

cards.question: A man skilled in his work won't stand before obscure men. He'll be stationed in the presence of ___.

cards.text: Next up, dinner with a ruler: consider carefully what is set before you, and if you possess a great appetite, put a knife to your throat. That is a STRONG way to say slow down, and I needed it every single time a batch came out of the oven.

cards.question: At the ruler's table, why shouldn't you crave his delicacies?

answers.text: That food is for his servants
That food is set aside for later

cards.text: The next saying is about money, and how hard to chase it.

cards.question: The teacher says it's worth wearing yourself out to get rich.

cards.text: Then comes a picture: "When you glance at wealth, it disappears, for it makes wings for itself and flies like an eagle to the sky." I've SEEN this, friend: it hits the account Friday, and by Sunday it's waving down from the clouds like BYE.

cards.question: What's the point of the picture of wealth flying off like an eagle?

answers.text: Riches come to whoever chases them
Riches grow when you watch them

cards.text: Next saying: do not eat the bread of a stingy man, and do not crave his delicacies.

cards.question: The stingy host tells you, 'Eat and drink.' What's really going on inside him?

answers.text: He's hoping you'll stay all night
He's getting ready to ask a favor

cards.text: His heart is not with you. It's the friend who says "Grab anything you want!" and then sends you a payment request for ONE cookie.

cards.question: At the stingy man's table, the teacher says even your pleasant words go to waste.

cards.text: Next saying: do not speak to a fool.

cards.question: Don't speak to a fool, for he will ___ the wisdom of your words.
The boundary stone warning comes back, with something added. Now it also says don't encroach on the fields of whom?
Why leave the fields of the fatherless alone? Who will take up their case against you?

cards.text: Then the teacher says, "Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge." Back at the start it was ear and mind, and now it's heart and ears.

cards.question: The last saying here turns to raising a child. The teacher says to hold back discipline from a child.

cards.text: The teacher says, "Strike him with a rod, and you will deliver his soul from Sheol." That's where we'll stop for now, friend, because these thirty sayings are nowhere near done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke 'not the guy in the back row pretending to take notes' is a classroom scene. Calling the speaker 'the teacher' makes the school reading stronger. Swap it for a work or everyday adult image, like a meeting or a group chat.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: The coupon joke doesn't click. A coupon has an offer, not a 'saying', so the comparison to thirty written sayings needs explaining. The added detail that the coupon 'expired before I got there' muddles the line further. It also adds a new fact to the drawer backstory instead of a small bakery moment.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The card spends its second sentence defining 'puts up security for debts' ('that's co-signing, putting your name on somebody else's loan'). The dictionary pop-up should handle this. Use the card words for the moment or for Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: Card 5 quotes the whole verse, including 'it disappears', and adds the joke 'waving down from the clouds like BYE'. That gives away card 6's answer, 'Riches don't stay with you'. One wrong answer, 'Riches grow when you watch them', is the exact opposite of the quoted 'When you glance at wealth, it disappears'. Fix it by holding back part of the picture on card 5 or by asking something card 5 hasn't stated.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Their uncles and cousins' is close to the right answer. In Israel a redeemer was a near relative (Lev 25:25, Ruth 3:12), so a baker could argue that relatives are the Redeemer who takes up the case. The right answer, 'Their strong Redeemer', also sounds more like the Bible than the other two answers.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Several story cards are bare restatements with no voice, most opening the same way. Examples: stop 1 card 7 ('Now the sayings begin. Do not rob...'), stop 1 card 13, stop 2 card 3 ('The next saying is about money...'), stop 2 card 7 ('Next saying: do not eat the bread...') and stop 2 card 11 ('Next saying: do not speak to a fool.'). The repeated 'Next saying' openings make the walkthrough read like a list instead of Papa Dorin moving the baker through it.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
